Petersenhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/blizzardscout1.html My favorite Dark Card. Enough said. Well, that would not make much of a card extra, would it? What combat vehicle is a staple of nearly every dark deck: the "Chicken Walker"! Take a look at the finalists decks from the 1997 World Championships, the mighty [[Blizzard Scout 1]] makes an appearance in both decks. Let's dissect this beauty. The [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the AT-ST which made an extremely brief sprint across the screen during the Empire Strikes Back. What they didn't tell you in the movie was that [[Darth Vader]] was being whisked to the Echo [[Cloud City: East Platform (Docking Bay){{!}}Docking Bay]], and, by the way, he trampled [[Major Bren Derlin]] on his way in to the hangar (Sorry Mr. Claven) [You see, [[Major Bren Derlin]] was talking to [[2-1B (Too-Onebee){{!}}2-1B]] about this snowman who was the spitting image of Richard Nixon.... TRAMPLE]. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the prototype of the Imperial's AT-ST cards which will come in Return of the Jedi expansions. This unique walker boasts everything you look for in a card. The Chicken Walker (named as such for its awkward look) is a natural in the mountains of [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] ([[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Mountains]], the [[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}6th Marker]]), where it deploys for 2 and has power 4, a great ratio. But wait, let's take a very typical game situation, [[Darth Vader]] is at the Defensive Perimeter waving his lightsaber at [[Commander Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] and Captain [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]]. Although they are out of sagacious gifts from the mentor or witty comments about not getting cocky (see the chicken theme), they decide to pick on our poor Dark Lord and initiate a battle. Well, Mr. [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]] just hops aboard his [[Blizzard Scout 1]] and reacts all the way over to join his comrade in arms. This interlude brings up the real benefits of [[Blizzard Scout 1]]. First, it boasts a landspeed of 3, the ability to react, a permanent pilot and a slot to fill with a pilot -- a great package deal. Remember there are several 3 ability Dark Side Pilots out there. Second, just look at that destiny, a 4! Perfect to keep your average destiny up, and pulling one of these as destiny for [[Trample]] will squash all of those pesky Light Side spies. (OK OK, if Obi, [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], [[Princess Leia]], [[BoShek]] or [[Yoda]] pull off [[Plastoid Armor]] and get [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] it will miss, but don't get technical with me!) Third, the walker is forfeit 5, a great way to soak up damage (just remember to lose the pilot first). Finally, there is also an S-comp link for good measure. Drawbacks. That is a tough one with the mighty Chicken Walker. But there are a couple. This walker does not have any immunity to attrition, despite its 4 armor rating. The other drawback is more of a reminder, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] does not count towards [[Walker Garrison]] as it is not an AT-AT. Forget that arrogant [[General Veers]] in his hulking [[Blizzard 1]], live life on the edge, blaze across the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] tundra in search of rebels to trample under foot with the all-powerful Chicken Waaaaalker! CARD COMBOS: [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations) = Keep your leader on the move to respond to battles. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Trample]] = Rebel Spies in the Lost Pile. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Boba Fett]] + [[Trample]] vs. [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] = Blizzard Scout 1 + [[Boba Fett]] vs. [[Han Solo]] (could have saved the imperials a lot on bribing [[Lando Calrissian (Dark){{!}}Lando Calrissian]]). [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites = With the vast number of [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is your all-purpose scout combat vehicle! |combos=* [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations).[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Blizzard%20Scout%201 Scomp: Blizzard Scout 1]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Decipher (Reflections foil)''' — [[Blizzard Scout 1 (Reflections Foil)|Blizzard Scout 1 (foil)]] |sources=* [[Blizzard Scout 1]] black-border printed face (3_156) * White-border product [[Revised Hoth]] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Vehicle: Blizzard Scout 1, Hoth, R1 * Printed face: [http://web.archive.org/web/20020327115743/http://decipher.com:80/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/images/blizzardscout1.gif Decipher.com card image] (Wayback copy of decipher.com/starwars/cardlists) |strategy=By Erik A. Petersen My favorite Dark Card. Enough said. Well, that would not make much of a card extra, would it? What combat vehicle is a staple of nearly every dark deck: the "Chicken Walker"! Take a look at the finalists decks from the 1997 World Championships, the mighty [[Blizzard Scout 1]] makes an appearance in both decks. Let's dissect this beauty. The [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the AT-ST which made an extremely brief sprint across the screen during the Empire Strikes Back. What they didn't tell you in the movie was that [[Darth Vader]] was being whisked to the Echo [[Cloud City: East Platform (Docking Bay){{!}}Docking Bay]], and, by the way, he trampled [[Major Bren Derlin]] on his way in to the hangar (Sorry Mr. Claven) [You see, [[Major Bren Derlin]] was talking to [[2-1B (Too-Onebee){{!}}2-1B]] about this snowman who was the spitting image of Richard Nixon.... TRAMPLE]. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the prototype of the Imperial's AT-ST cards which will come in Return of the Jedi expansions. This unique walker boasts everything you look for in a card. The Chicken Walker (named as such for its awkward look) is a natural in the mountains of [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] ([[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Mountains]], the [[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}6th Marker]]), where it deploys for 2 and has power 4, a great ratio. But wait, let's take a very typical game situation, [[Darth Vader]] is at the Defensive Perimeter waving his lightsaber at [[Commander Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] and Captain [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]]. Although they are out of sagacious gifts from the mentor or witty comments about not getting cocky (see the chicken theme), they decide to pick on our poor Dark Lord and initiate a battle. Well, Mr. [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]] just hops aboard his [[Blizzard Scout 1]] and reacts all the way over to join his comrade in arms. This interlude brings up the real benefits of [[Blizzard Scout 1]]. First, it boasts a landspeed of 3, the ability to react, a permanent pilot and a slot to fill with a pilot -- a great package deal. Remember there are several 3 ability Dark Side Pilots out there. Second, just look at that destiny, a 4! Perfect to keep your average destiny up, and pulling one of these as destiny for [[Trample]] will squash all of those pesky Light Side spies. (OK OK, if Obi, [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], [[Princess Leia]], [[BoShek]] or [[Yoda]] pull off [[Plastoid Armor]] and get [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] it will miss, but don't get technical with me!) Third, the walker is forfeit 5, a great way to soak up damage (just remember to lose the pilot first). Finally, there is also an S-comp link for good measure. Drawbacks. That is a tough one with the mighty Chicken Walker. But there are a couple. This walker does not have any immunity to attrition, despite its 4 armor rating. The other drawback is more of a reminder, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] does not count towards [[Walker Garrison]] as it is not an AT-AT. Forget that arrogant [[General Veers]] in his hulking [[Blizzard 1]], live life on the edge, blaze across the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] tundra in search of rebels to trample under foot with the all-powerful Chicken Waaaaalker! CARD COMBOS: [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations) = Keep your leader on the move to respond to battles. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Trample]] = Rebel Spies in the Lost Pile. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Boba Fett]] + [[Trample]] vs. [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] = Blizzard Scout 1 + [[Boba Fett]] vs. [[Han Solo]] (could have saved the imperials a lot on bribing [[Lando Calrissian (Dark){{!}}Lando Calrissian]]). [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites = With the vast number of [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is your all-purpose scout combat vehicle! |combos=* [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations). * [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Trample]] [[Trample]] opponent's undercover spies. * [[Battle Deployment]] * [[Veers (V)]] |also_known_as=* Chicken Walker }}

Target hit and forfeit =0, if destiny matches target's destiny number). |errata_history=This is errata version PC-E1 of [[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V)]] (version 2 of 4). This version has no document image of its own, so the image here is a CardMaker recreation of this text ([[:File:VB8-03-Bossk_With_Mortar_Gun-PC-E1-cardmaker.png]]). Versions in date order: [[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V)]] (original, release sheet of 11 May 2012); '''this page''' (PC-E1, PC website card list, by 21 July 2012); [[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V) (Errata 2)]] (PC-E2, Master List of 27 April 2013, the same words as the original); [[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V) (Errata 3)]] (PC-E3, Players Committee card image, uploaded 7 May 2013, the same words as the original, the current text). * '''Original''' ([[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V)]]): text as given in the Virtual Block 8.1 release sheet[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock8_1.pdf#page=2 Virtual Block 8.1 release sheet] ("Official text as of May 11, 2012"; this copy was re-made on 18 July 2012), page 2, slip 4 (position on the sheet; the slip prints no number). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027095418/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock8_1.pdf#page=2 Internet Archive]: “Adds 2 to power of anything he pilots. May not be targeted by weapons unless your other slavers present are each ‘hit.’ Permanent weapon is •Bossk's Mortar Gun (may target a character for free; draw destiny; target hit, and its forfeit = 0, if destiny = target's destiny number).” The release-sheet slip ([[:File:VB8-03-Bossk_With_Mortar_Gun.png]]) and the Players Committee card image ([[:File:VB8-D-bosskwithmortargun-pre.gif]]) print it. The Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (official text as of 27 April 2013) prints this text again[[Media:Virtual_Legacy_Final_Master_DS.pdf|Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (Dark Side)]], cover "official text as of April 27, 2013" (PDF built February 2014). Original: http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterDS.pdf#page=5, page 5. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170704232650/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterDS.pdf#page=5 Internet Archive]; under the ruling of 11 November 2026 (every publication is a version), that copy is its own version, PC-E2 ([[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V) (Errata 2)]]); the current text is the PC card image uploaded on 7 May 2013 ([[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V) (Errata 3)]], the same words). The release-sheet slip prints no slip number. * '''PC-E1''' (this page): the PC website card list (shown there by 21 July 2012, the earliest archived capture with text, and in every capture to 11 January 2013) has “each 'hit'. Permanent” instead of “each ‘hit.’ Permanent”, “(may target a character for free. Draw destiny. Target hit and forfeit =0, if destiny matches target's destiny number)” instead of “(may target a character for free; draw destiny; target hit, and its forfeit = 0, if destiny = target's destiny number)” (the pilot icon written out as “Adds 2 to the power of anything he pilots.”)Players Committee website card list (VBlock8Type), as captured [https://web.archive.org/web/20120721064747/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/cardlists/VBlock8Type.html 2012-07-21] (Internet Archive); same text in every capture to [https://web.archive.org/web/20130111142925/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/cardlists/VBlock8Type.html 2013-01-11]: “Adds 2 to the power of anything he pilots. May not be targeted by weapons unless your other slavers present are each 'hit'. Permanent weapon is •Bossk's Mortar Gun (may target a character for free. Draw destiny. Target hit and forfeit =0, if destiny matches target's destiny number).” No published card image shows this text; the image of that page is a CardMaker recreation ([[:File:VB8-03-Bossk_With_Mortar_Gun-PC-E1-cardmaker.png]]). The card list was generated from the Players Committee's Holotable card data (research R7, 11 November 2026), so this wording is a transcription the PC published, not a separately announced errata; it is listed because it was published. * '''PC-E2''' ([[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V) (Errata 2)]]): the Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (official text as of 27 April 2013; Dark Side, p. 5) prints the original release-sheet text ([[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V)]]) again, word for word: “Adds 2 to power of anything he pilots. May not be targeted by weapons unless your other slavers present are each ‘hit.’ Permanent weapon is •Bossk's Mortar Gun (may target a character for free; draw destiny; target hit, and its forfeit = 0, if destiny = target's destiny number).” It is listed as a version because it was published (ruling of 11 November 2026: every publication is a version, even a word-for-word repeat of an earlier text); the PC card image uploaded later ([[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V) (Errata 3)]]) is the current text. Its image is the Master List slip ([[:File:VL-history-1281-4-front-master.png]]). The Master List slip prints no slip number, like the release-sheet slip and the PC card image. * '''PC-E3''' ([[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V) (Errata 3)]]): the Players Committee card image ([[:File:VB8-D-bosskwithmortargun-pre.gif]]) prints the original release-sheet text ([[Bossk With Mortar Gun (V)]]) again, word for word: “Adds 2 to power of anything he pilots. May not be targeted by weapons unless your other slavers present are each ‘hit.’ Permanent weapon is •Bossk's Mortar Gun (may target a character for free; draw destiny; target hit, and its forfeit = 0, if destiny = target's destiny number).” The image is dated only by its upload to the Players Committee's server: the Apache listing of the Virtual8-Dark card-image folder gives every file there the same time, 7 May 2013, 13:52Players Committee server, [https://web.archive.org/web/20190818034744/https://starwarsccg.org/cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual8-Dark/large/?C=M;O=A directory listing of cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual8-Dark/large/] sorted by date, as captured 18 August 2019 (Internet Archive). That is a bulk upload date, so the image may have been made earlier; it is placed at that date (ruling of 11 November 2026: what was uploaded last counts as the last version). It is listed as a version because it was published (ruling of 11 November 2026: every publication is a version, even a word-for-word repeat). Uploaded after the Master List, it is the latest version and so the current text. '''Title'''
Luke Skywalker, Lieutenant Colonel
'''Lore'''
Hero of the Battle of Yavin. Over these three years, he gained experience as a soldier of the Alliance, and his current rank is lieutenant colonel. At the Battle of Hoth, he served as the leader of Echo Base's flight squadron.
'''Game text'''
May deploy only on Hoth, but may move anywhere afterward. Adds 3 to the power of a starship he pilots. If piloting Rogue 1, adds 2 to maneuver. Immune to attrition < 3. All other Rogue Squadron pilots and gunners at the same Hoth location have forfeit +1.
The Japanese title and lore use 中佐, a rank term translated as lieutenant colonel or, in naval usage, commander; the English printing uses Commander. '''Decipher Errata''' — [[Djas Puhr (Errata)]] (1_171) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/index.html Premiere Dark Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002) * Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/djaspuhr.html Djas Puhr], [[Decipher]] (archived 4 August 2002). * Printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/images/djaspuhr.gif Decipher.com card image] (Wayback copy of decipher.com/starwars/cardlists) |strategy=By Kevin LaPortehttps://web.archive.org/web/20021114054006/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/djaspuhr.html So, I'm perusing the Premiere card list, looking for a card to write an extra for, and I happen upon one of my favorite characters since the game was released: [[Djas Puhr]]...and I realize that nobody's bothered to write an extra for him! Yeah, I couldn't believe it either. The Sakiyan bounty hunter is an underused powerhouse, for fairly obvious reasons. Ability = 4 is one big reason: any card that draws battle destiny on its own speaks for itself. Add to that [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]'s immunity to attrition < 3, and you've got a guy who can draw his own destiny AND potentially avoid falling victim to the attrition of his enemies. Can you think of any other characters with such abilities? Do the names [[Darth Vader]], [[Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], or [[Princess Leia]] ring a bell? Djas does appear to have one glaring weakness upon first glance: Power = 1, but take another look at his game text: Power +1 for each DS icon present, +2 under "nighttime conditions." Ouch...drop [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]] at any DS location with two DS icons, and he's Power = 3. Add a [[Presence Of The Force]], and he's Power = 4. Make that DS location the [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]], and he's Power = 5. Play [[Sunsdown]] on [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]...forget about it...Power = 8...my man is ragin': "The [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] is MY house!!!" But it doesn't end there: this guy is rife with combo potential. Let's go back to his Ability = 4. Not only can he utilize the Dark Jedi abilities of [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]] and [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] with some proficiency, but also: can you say, "[[Weapon Levitation]]?" That's right: "I'll take that lightsaber, Mr. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Kenobi]]." What's that? You say you don't use [[Weapon Levitation]]? (Well, you should!) Just give Djas (a warrior, by the way) his own [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]]...only 3 Force to deploy and target (much less than most DS characters), and he has as much chance to hit Rebels and their co-conspirators as [[Lord Vader]] himself. The lightsaber combos that follow go without saying ([[All Too Easy]], [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]], [[You Are Beaten]], etc., etc.). Also, want to add a little extra attrition to your damage with [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]? Try [[Res Luk Ra'auf]], adding a battle destiny for a bounty hunter defending alone, giving Djas and his Ability = 4 not one, but TWO battle destiny draws. This list goes on, but you get the picture...[[Djas Puhr]], Sakiyan bounty hunter, ROCKS. He is a must in most DS ground decks and can really show his stuff when the LS spreads their forces thin to force drain and leaves characters with less than Ability = 4 at a site. Next time you need some hired ground muscle (and one heck of a tracker), call on [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]. Combos: Djas + [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] + [[Presence Of The Force]] = Power of 5, Immunity to Attrition < 3, and a destiny draw. Djas + [[Weapon Levitation]] = one less unique LS lightsaber to worry about...and one more for you to USE. Djas + [[Res Luk Ra'auf]] = 2 battle destiny. Djas + [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]] = BACK OFF!!! |rulings=* This card is not an assassin. |combos=* [[Djas Puhr]] + [[Res Luk Ra'auf]]https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Djas%20Puhr. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024020140/https://swccg.com/snapshots/scomp/djas-puhr.html Internet Archive] |pulled_by=* [[Double Back]] |characteristics=* Force-Sensitive * Black Sun agent * bounty hunter * Sakiyan |underlying_card_for=* [[Djas Puhr (V)]] |has_refs=1 }}

Yeah, I couldn't believe it either. The Sakiyan bounty hunter is an underused powerhouse, for fairly obvious reasons. Ability = 4 is one big reason: any card that draws battle destiny on its own speaks for itself. Add to that [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]'s immunity to attrition < 3, and you've got a guy who can draw his own destiny AND potentially avoid falling victim to the attrition of his enemies. Can you think of any other characters with such abilities? Do the names [[Darth Vader]], [[Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], or [[Princess Leia]] ring a bell? Djas does appear to have one glaring weakness upon first glance: Power = 1, but take another look at his game text: Power +1 for each DS icon present, +2 under "nighttime conditions." Ouch...drop [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]] at any DS location with two DS icons, and he's Power = 3. Add a [[Presence Of The Force]], and he's Power = 4. Make that DS location the [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]], and he's Power = 5. Play [[Sunsdown]] on [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]...forget about it...Power = 8...my man is ragin': "The [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] is MY house!!!" But it doesn't end there: this guy is rife with combo potential. Let's go back to his Ability = 4. Not only can he utilize the Dark Jedi abilities of [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]] and [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] with some proficiency, but also: can you say, "[[Weapon Levitation]]?" That's right: "I'll take that lightsaber, Mr. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Kenobi]]." What's that? You say you don't use [[Weapon Levitation]]? (Well, you should!) Just give Djas (a warrior, by the way) his own [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]]...only 3 Force to deploy and target (much less than most DS characters), and he has as much chance to hit Rebels and their co-conspirators as [[Lord Vader]] himself. The lightsaber combos that follow go without saying ([[All Too Easy]], [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]], [[You Are Beaten]], etc., etc.). Also, want to add a little extra attrition to your damage with [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]? Try [[Res Luk Ra'auf]], adding a battle destiny for a bounty hunter defending alone, giving Djas and his Ability = 4 not one, but TWO battle destiny draws. This list goes on, but you get the picture...[[Djas Puhr]], Sakiyan bounty hunter, ROCKS. He is a must in most DS ground decks and can really show his stuff when the LS spreads their forces thin to force drain and leaves characters with less than Ability = 4 at a site. Next time you need some hired ground muscle (and one heck of a tracker), call on [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]. Combos: Djas + [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] + [[Presence Of The Force]] = Power of 5, Immunity to Attrition < 3, and a destiny draw. Djas + [[Weapon Levitation]] = one less unique LS lightsaber to worry about...and one more for you to USE. Djas + [[Res Luk Ra'auf]] = 2 battle destiny. Djas + [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]] = BACK OFF!!! |rulings=* This card is not an assassin. |combos=* [[Djas Puhr]] + [[Res Luk Ra'auf]]https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Djas%20Puhr. '''Decipher (Reflections II foil)''' — [[Echo Base Operations (Reflections II Foil)|Echo Base Operations (foil)]] |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Effect: Echo Base Operations, Hoth, R2 |strategy=By Carl "Mike" Hardyhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/light/small/echobaseoperations.html Well, this card needs little introduction. I remember when I got my first Box of the [[Hoth (location){{!}}Hoth]] expansion and got a look at this card. I thought, "Wow, I wonder if I could make this work...." Well, I read into it and decided that it would simply be too hard to make happen and frankly kind of susceptible to more "specialized" decks. Boy, was I wrong! A few months later the [[Echo Base Operations]] (EBO) deck burst onto the scene. It was fast, it was tough, and it was nearly unstoppable! To be honest, I believe this card to be the second most powerful non-character card in the game (second only to the quite effective, and dreaded, [[Scanning Crew]]). Here's how it works. To most effectively use EBO you've got to get the necessary sites on the table. This can be made easier if you have two of each of these needed sites. Also, have plenty of System Location through which to drain from. The main idea isn't to battle - don't let that "+3 in battle" fool you. The most efficient EBO decks I've seen have only Y-wings (which deploy for nothing with EBO in place) and protective interrupts like [[Hyper Escape]] or [[Houjix]]. Once the Dark Side commits to an action with EBO going, you'll be able to drain your dark opponent out of the game before he can mount another such action. : *Echo Base Command Center + Droid + How Did We Get Into This Mess = You can go through your deck and get everything you need in only a couple of turns. This makes an otherwise slow EBO deck, insanely fast! *EBO + [[Kessel]] + 3 Y-wings + [[Y-wing Assault Squadron]] = With EBO running you can deploy the Y-wings for nothing at [[Kessel]] and replace them with the Squadron. Your drains are now 5 at [[Kessel]]! Few cards can get you that kind of game-impacting potential! : 9.5 (I would have given it a 10 except for the fact that by and large EBO decks are suceptible to Monnock.) |combos=* [[Echo Base Operations]] + Echo Base Command Center + any Droid + [[How Did We Get Into This Mess?]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Echo%20Base%20Operations Scomp: Echo Base Operations]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020174249/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json Internet Archive] * [[Echo Base Operations]] + [[Kessel]] + 3 Y-wings + [[Y-wing Assault Squadron]] |pulled_by=* [[A New Secret Base]] * [[The Signal]] * [[We Wish To Board At Once]] * [[Wokling (V)]] |also_known_as=* EBO |has_refs=1 }}

'''Virtual Modern''' — [[Djas Puhr (V)]] (201_24) |sources=* Recreation of the Decipher.com Premiere Limited scan: white rounded border, transparent corners, same pixel size. * [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/index.html Premiere Dark Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Djas Puhr, Premiere, R2 |strategy=By Kevin LaPortehttps://web.archive.org/web/20021114054006/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/djaspuhr.html So, I'm perusing the Premiere card list, looking for a card to write an extra for, and I happen upon one of my favorite characters since the game was released: [[Djas Puhr]]...and I realize that nobody's bothered to write an extra for him! Yeah, I couldn't believe it either. The Sakiyan bounty hunter is an underused powerhouse, for fairly obvious reasons. Ability = 4 is one big reason: any card that draws battle destiny on its own speaks for itself. Add to that [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]'s immunity to attrition < 3, and you've got a guy who can draw his own destiny AND potentially avoid falling victim to the attrition of his enemies. Can you think of any other characters with such abilities? Do the names [[Darth Vader]], [[Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], or [[Princess Leia]] ring a bell? Djas does appear to have one glaring weakness upon first glance: Power = 1, but take another look at his game text: Power +1 for each DS icon present, +2 under "nighttime conditions." Ouch...drop [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]] at any DS location with two DS icons, and he's Power = 3. Add a [[Presence Of The Force]], and he's Power = 4. Make that DS location the [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]], and he's Power = 5. Play [[Sunsdown]] on [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]...forget about it...Power = 8...my man is ragin': "The [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] is MY house!!!" But it doesn't end there: this guy is rife with combo potential. Let's go back to his Ability = 4. Not only can he utilize the Dark Jedi abilities of [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]] and [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] with some proficiency, but also: can you say, "[[Weapon Levitation]]?" That's right: "I'll take that lightsaber, Mr. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Kenobi]]." What's that? You say you don't use [[Weapon Levitation]]? (Well, you should!) Just give Djas (a warrior, by the way) his own [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]]...only 3 Force to deploy and target (much less than most DS characters), and he has as much chance to hit Rebels and their co-conspirators as [[Lord Vader]] himself. The lightsaber combos that follow go without saying ([[All Too Easy]], [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]], [[You Are Beaten]], etc., etc.). Also, want to add a little extra attrition to your damage with [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]? Try [[Res Luk Ra'auf]], adding a battle destiny for a bounty hunter defending alone, giving Djas and his Ability = 4 not one, but TWO battle destiny draws. This list goes on, but you get the picture...[[Djas Puhr]], Sakiyan bounty hunter, ROCKS. He is a must in most DS ground decks and can really show his stuff when the LS spreads their forces thin to force drain and leaves characters with less than Ability = 4 at a site. Next time you need some hired ground muscle (and one heck of a tracker), call on [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]. Combos: Djas + [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] + [[Presence Of The Force]] = Power of 5, Immunity to Attrition < 3, and a destiny draw. Djas + [[Weapon Levitation]] = one less unique LS lightsaber to worry about...and one more for you to USE. Djas + [[Res Luk Ra'auf]] = 2 battle destiny. Djas + [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]] = BACK OFF!!! |rulings=* This card is not an assassin. |combos=* [[Djas Puhr]] + [[Res Luk Ra'auf]]https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Djas%20Puhr. '''Decipher (Reflections II foil)''' — [[Echo Base Operations (Reflections II Foil)|Echo Base Operations (foil)]] |sources=* [[Echo Base Operations]] black-border printed face (3_34) * White-border product [[Revised Hoth]] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Effect: Echo Base Operations, Hoth, R2 |strategy=By Carl "Mike" Hardy Well, this card needs little introduction. I remember when I got my first Box of the [[Hoth (location){{!}}Hoth]] expansion and got a look at this card. I thought, "Wow, I wonder if I could make this work...." Well, I read into it and decided that it would simply be too hard to make happen and frankly kind of susceptible to more "specialized" decks. Boy, was I wrong! A few months later the [[Echo Base Operations]] (EBO) deck burst onto the scene. It was fast, it was tough, and it was nearly unstoppable! To be honest, I believe this card to be the second most powerful non-character card in the game (second only to the quite effective, and dreaded, [[Scanning Crew]]). Here's how it works. To most effectively use EBO you've got to get the necessary sites on the table. This can be made easier if you have two of each of these needed sites. Also, have plenty of System Location through which to drain from. The main idea isn't to battle - don't let that "+3 in battle" fool you. The most efficient EBO decks I've seen have only Y-wings (which deploy for nothing with EBO in place) and protective interrupts like [[Hyper Escape]] or [[Houjix]]. Once the Dark Side commits to an action with EBO going, you'll be able to drain your dark opponent out of the game before he can mount another such action. : *Echo Base Command Center + Droid + How Did We Get Into This Mess = You can go through your deck and get everything you need in only a couple of turns. This makes an otherwise slow EBO deck, insanely fast! *EBO + [[Kessel]] + 3 Y-wings + [[Y-wing Assault Squadron]] = With EBO running you can deploy the Y-wings for nothing at [[Kessel]] and replace them with the Squadron. Your drains are now 5 at [[Kessel]]! Few cards can get you that kind of game-impacting potential! : 9.5 (I would have given it a 10 except for the fact that by and large EBO decks are suceptible to Monnock.) |combos=* [[Echo Base Operations]] + Echo Base Command Center + any Droid + [[How Did We Get Into This Mess?]] * [[Echo Base Operations]] + [[Kessel]] + 3 Y-wings + [[Y-wing Assault Squadron]] * [[The Signal]] * [[We Wish To Board At Once]] * [[Wokling (V)]] |also_known_as=* EBO }}

Your [[Maul]], aliens (except Mara), [Independent Starship] starships, and senators are lost. [Immune to Alter] |errata_history=This is the original printed text (version 1 of 4). The image here is the release-sheet slip that prints it. The current text is [[Expand The Empire (V) (Errata 3)]] (PC-E3): the Master List of 27 April 2013. The PC card image ([[Expand The Empire (V) (Errata 2)]], PC-E2) and the Master List both print this text again word for word. * '''Original''' (this page): text as given in the Virtual Block 5 release sheet (official text as of 7 December 2009): “Deploy on Senate. May raise your converted Senate to the top. Jedi here are politics +4. While your total politics here is > 5, at battlegrounds where you have an Imperial, your Force drains and battle destiny draws are +1. Your Maul, aliens (except Mara), [Independent Starship] starships, and senators are lost. (Immune to Alter.)”.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock5.pdf#page=2 Virtual Block 5 release sheet] ("Official text as of 7 December 2009"), page 2, slip 18. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027095234/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock5.pdf#page=2 Internet Archive] Document: the release-sheet slip ([[:File:VB5-18-Expand_The_Empire.png]]) prints slip number “18” bottom right. * '''PC-E1''' ([[Expand The Empire (V) (Errata)]]): The PC website card list (shown there by 21 July 2012, the earliest archived capture with text, and in every capture to 11 January 2013) reordered the list of lost cards: “Your Maul, aliens (except Mara), [Independent Starship] starships, and senators are lost” became “Your aliens (except Mara), senators, Maul, and [Independent Starship] starships are lost”. PC-E1 text: “Deploy on Senate. May raise your converted Senate to the top. Jedi here are politics +4. While your total politics here is > 5, at battlegrounds where you have an Imperial, your Force drains and battle destiny draws are +1. Your aliens (except Mara), senators, Maul, and [Independent Starship] starships are lost. (Immune to Alter.)”Players Committee website card list (VBlock5Type), as captured [https://web.archive.org/web/20120721064732/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/cardlists/VBlock5Type.html 2012-07-21] (Internet Archive) The PC website card list was generated from the Players Committee's Holotable card data (research R7, 11 November 2026), so its wording follows that data; it is listed as a version because the PC published it. * '''PC-E2''' ([[Expand The Empire (V) (Errata 2)]]): Players Committee card image ([[:File:VB5-D-expandtheempire-pre.gif]]), on the PC website by 25 February 2013 (server upload date)Players Committee card image, file cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual5-Dark/large/expandtheempire.gif; the directory listing of this folder (Virtual5-Dark) was not captured; the captured Legacy folders (Virtual2, Virtual4, Virtual5, Virtual6, Virtual7) all carry 25-Feb-2013 11:33/11:34, the date the PC rebuilt its image set (research R6, 11 November 2026: these are bulk upload dates, and an image may have been made earlier). Today's copy: https://res.starwarsccg.org/cards/legacy/VirtualBlock5-Dark/large/expandtheempire.gif: “Deploy on Senate. May raise your converted Senate to the top. Jedi here are politics +4. While your total politics here is > 5, at battlegrounds where you have an Imperial, your Force drains and battle destiny draws are +1. Your Maul, aliens (except Mara), [Independent Starship] starships, and senators are lost. [Immune to Alter]” '''What changed:''' the PC card image prints the original release-sheet text of 7 December 2009 again, word for word, after the PC website card list (PC-E1) had published a different text. It is listed as its own version, placed at its upload date (Bill's rulings of 11 November 2026: a PC card image is its own version, placed at its date (here its server upload date), even when its words repeat an earlier version; whatever was published last is current). The date is only the folder's bulk upload date: the image may have been made earlier, so its place in the order is uncertain, but the versioning order follows the upload date. Document: the PC card image is a whole card (art, title bar, lore, icons, frame and the Virtual Block 5 set mark) and prints the number “18” bottom right, as the release-sheet slip does. * '''PC-E3''' ([[Expand The Empire (V) (Errata 3)]]): Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (Dark Side p. 25), official text as of 27 April 2013[[Media:Virtual_Legacy_Final_Master_DS.pdf|Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (Dark Side)]], cover "official text as of April 27, 2013" (PDF built February 2014). Original: http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterDS.pdf#page=25, page 25. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170704232650/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterDS.pdf#page=25 Internet Archive]: “Deploy on Senate. May raise your converted Senate to the top. Jedi here are politics +4. While your total politics here is > 5, at battlegrounds where you have an Imperial, your Force drains and battle destiny draws are +1. Your Maul, aliens (except Mara), [Independent Starship] starships, and senators are lost. [Immune to Alter]” '''What changed:''' the Master List prints the original release-sheet text of 7 December 2009 again, word for word. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. '''Decipher (Revised)''' — [[General Veers (Revised)]] (53_87) |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (General Veers; November 1998) * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/generalveers.html [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. The shield generators will be down in moments, you may start your landing. |pulled_by=* [[Blizzard 4]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=General%20Veers Scomp: General Veers]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020174249/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json Internet Archive] * [[Imperial Command]] |matching=* [[Blizzard 1]] |personas=* [[General Veers (persona)|Veers]] |characteristics=* Force-Attuned * general * leader |underlying_card_for=* [[General Veers (V)]] |has_refs=1 |notes=* Decipher [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998) revised game text. '''Decipher (Reflections foil)''' — [[General Veers (Reflections Foil)|General Veers (foil)]] |sources=* [[General Veers]] black-border printed face (3_87) * White-border product [[Revised Hoth]] * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4 [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. The shield generators will be down in moments, you may start your landing. * [[Imperial Command]] * general * leader * [[General Veers]] }}

'''Virtual Modern Errata''' — [[Greedo (V) (Errata)]] (204_42) — current |sources=* Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080512224452/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/greedo.html Greedo], [[Decipher]] (archived 12 May 2008). * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Greedo, A New Hope, R1 |strategy=By Tom Landyhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/greedo.html [[Greedo]] isn't the greatest alien. In fact, nearly everybody says that his card isn't even worth space in a deck. But, in some cases, he can really be useful. At a deploy cost of one, this bounty hunter's power is two, his ability is one, his destiny is two, but his forfeit is only a half. [[Greedo]] also possesses a special ability which allows him to "threaten" Smugglers. His game text says: " During opponent's control phase, may "threaten" one smuggler at same site. Opponent may use all force pile cards to cancel "threat", allowing you to activate the same amount. Otherwise, draw destiny. If destiny plus [[Greedo]]'s ability is >6, smuggler is lost." Now I know what you are thinking. "Why would anyone use [[Greedo]]? His forfeit stinks, and to kill a smuggler, the destiny must be a six!" While all of this is true, there are always ways to improve things. For instance, to improve his forfeit, keep him around the dark side's [[Tatooine: Mos Eisley (Dark){{!}}Tatooine: Mos Eisley]]. Here, [[Greedo]]'s forfeit would get a plus one bonus, and his power would be three. Another quick way to boost his forfeit is to slap a [[Stormtrooper Utility Belt]] around his waist. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit and power would both get a plus one bonus, but if he was on the [[Death Star]], the bonus would be plus two. Now, a forfeit of two and a half isn't bad. If you have a lot of destinies of six in your deck, you will be able to "threaten" major smugglers like [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]], [[Chewbacca]], and even [[Wedge Antilles]] easily if you have certain cards that will help you. An [[Electrobinoculars]] would be ideal to locate destinies of six, if only the dark side had this device. So, use [[Reegesk]], [[Tonnika Sisters]] or any other way to steal them from your opponent. [[Electrobinoculars]] is a very popular and powerful card, so you don't have to really worry about your opponent not having them. Another good way to find destinies that you need is with [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]]. When at a scomp link, [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]] enables you to peek at the top three cards of your reserve deck during your draw phase for one force. By knowing what your destiny is, even if it isn't a six, you can still bluff because your opponent won't know if you are lying or not. Trained by bounty hunters Nataz and Goa, who betrayed him to Thuku. |game_text=During opponent's control phase, may 'threaten' one smuggler at same site. If destiny + Greedo's ability > 6, smuggler lost. |printings='''Decipher''' — [[Greedo]] (2_89)
'''Decipher (Revised)''' — '''this page''' (52_89)
'''Decipher (Reflections foil)''' — [[Greedo (Reflections Foil)|Greedo (foil)]] |sources=* [[Greedo]] black-border printed face (2_89) * White-border product [[Revised A New Hope]] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Greedo, A New Hope, R1 |strategy=By Tom Landy [[Greedo]] isn't the greatest alien. In fact, nearly everybody says that his card isn't even worth space in a deck. But, in some cases, he can really be useful. At a deploy cost of one, this bounty hunter's power is two, his ability is one, his destiny is two, but his forfeit is only a half. [[Greedo]] also possesses a special ability which allows him to "threaten" Smugglers. His game text says: " During opponent's control phase, may "threaten" one smuggler at same site. Opponent may use all force pile cards to cancel "threat", allowing you to activate the same amount. Otherwise, draw destiny. If destiny plus [[Greedo]]'s ability is >6, smuggler is lost." Now I know what you are thinking. "Why would anyone use [[Greedo]]? His forfeit stinks, and to kill a smuggler, the destiny must be a six!" While all of this is true, there are always ways to improve things. For instance, to improve his forfeit, keep him around the dark side's [[Tatooine: Mos Eisley (Dark){{!}}Tatooine: Mos Eisley]]. Here, [[Greedo]]'s forfeit would get a plus one bonus, and his power would be three. Another quick way to boost his forfeit is to slap a [[Stormtrooper Utility Belt]] around his waist. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit and power would both get a plus one bonus, but if he was on the [[Death Star]], the bonus would be plus two. Now, a forfeit of two and a half isn't bad. If you have a lot of destinies of six in your deck, you will be able to "threaten" major smugglers like [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]], [[Chewbacca]], and even [[Wedge Antilles]] easily if you have certain cards that will help you. An [[Electrobinoculars]] would be ideal to locate destinies of six, if only the dark side had this device. So, use [[Reegesk]], [[Tonnika Sisters]] or any other way to steal them from your opponent. [[Electrobinoculars]] is a very popular and powerful card, so you don't have to really worry about your opponent not having them. Another good way to find destinies that you need is with [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]]. When at a scomp link, [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]] enables you to peek at the top three cards of your reserve deck during your draw phase for one force. By knowing what your destiny is, even if it isn't a six, you can still bluff because your opponent won't know if you are lying or not. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit value and special ability to "threaten" smugglers aren't great, but when combined with certain cards it can really be helpful. * [[Greeata]] * bounty hunter * Rodian }}

Target hit, and forfeit = 0, if total destiny > defense value.” The image is dated only by its upload to the Players Committee's server: the Apache listing of the Virtual8-Dark card-image folder gives every file there the same time, 7 May 2013, 13:52Players Committee server, [https://web.archive.org/web/20190818034744/https://starwarsccg.org/cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual8-Dark/large/?C=M;O=A directory listing of cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual8-Dark/large/] sorted by date, as captured 18 August 2019 (Internet Archive). '''Decipher Errata''' — [[Presence Of The Force (Errata)]] (1_227) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/index.html Premiere Dark Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002) * Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/presenceoftheforce.html Presence Of The Force], [[Decipher]] (archived 4 August 2002). * Printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/images/presenceoftheforce.gif Decipher.com card image] (Wayback copy of decipher.com/starwars/cardlists) |strategy=By Justin Pakeshttps://web.archive.org/web/20001010191601/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/presenceoftheforce.html Imagine my dismay as I browsed the voluminous libraries of Deciphers card lists to discover that one of my favourite (proper English spelling there... :) cards was sans card extra. The often acronymed, PotF. So lets see if I can add anything to even that score. Being a Premiere card, the old hands amongst you may not find anything new here, but then again, maybe a refresher is in order. The card adds one red and one blue Force icon to whatever location you deploy it. A sabre for me, and a sabre for you. The deploy is zero as are the deployment restrictions. It's a two dot card, but remember that "cumulativity" stops you gaining any benefits from two copies at the same location. The wonderous thing about this card is it's elegant simplicity but amazing versatility. One use of the card is a boon to the early game. It is an extra Force activated. And in that frustrating game where the only time you see your locations is as destiny draws, that extra one can be vital. The most obvious offensive use of this card is immediately apparent, a bigger drain at a location, preferably one you already securely control! Lovely for you, added headache for your opponent! And never forget that it is *any* location. Handy if your opponent forgot to stock Cloud Cars and your trying to boost the benefit of your cloud superiority! "Just another drain bonus" some of you are saying, I can get that with a sabre! But with the advent of [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], the true value of a PotF used in this way was realised. Being an extra icon, and NOT a drain bonus (such as +1 to Force Drains) it is immune to that 'Bane of the Drain', [[Great Warrior]] (Jedi Test #1). The alternate use is a little more subtle. At a location where you have no force icons, this card is better than a spy. Sure, it can't go undercover, but it won't get snipered by the first weapon that comes along either. That extra icon allows you normal deploy, and is like the front door key to many LS starting locations. E.g. Massasi [[Hoth: Echo Command Center (War Room){{!}}War Room]], Obi's Hut, [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] Echo Base Command Centre (before the shields go up), or even LS [[Dantooine (Dark){{!}}Dantooine]]. If you can get the power down you need to hold them, that makes for a big early drain. If you have it in hand really early, it can be your only hope against those irritating LS decks that revolve your starting location early depriving you of force. Even better, allow yourself to get to that LS Big One and cancel that darned Asteroid Sanctuary. There are also a few more esoteric uses. A couple of cards are concerned with the number of icons at a location. [[Djas Puhr]], [[Feltipern Trevagg]], or even [[Commence Primary Ignition]] for a little added destruction. I would also say Braniac, but when it comes to that sort of mathematical proficiency, I'm a weak-minded fool. ;) "The perfect all round card!" I hear you now exclaim. Surely there's a catch! And indeed there is. But to me, the quality that makes this a *great* card is how it is a double-edged sabre if you use it without thinking. Very appopriate when you consider the picture on the card. Play it early, and you could be giving your opponent much needed Force activation. Put it on a location you cannot hold, and you may well feel the sting of the extra drain. Without proper planninng and situational analysis, many of the benefits could end up benefitting the Light Side. This tool belongs to the thinking player. And beware the counters too. Cloud City's Clash Of Sabres will cancel it outright. [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] has the same effect, but there's plenty of counter-counter's to that. And most irritating of all is [[I Have A Bad Feeling About This]] which LS can use to retarget it to a location they control (e.g. [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]!). I always recommend the multi-function [[Bad Feeling Have I]] to take care of that problem. Combos: How can you list combos for something that can be used almost anywhere, anytime? Obvious => PotF + LS Obi's Hut + your characters controlling it with a Vaders sabre and a Dark Jedi Sabre = drain of 6. Favourite => PotF + DS Mos Eisley + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Djas Puhr]] = An alien who even alone is Power 8, Ability 4, Forfeit 5, Immune To Attrition < 3, draws destiny, and gets an extra destiny worth of power! Even [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] would quietly thank the Emperor that he's on the right side of that behemoth! For icing on the attrition cake, add [[Lone Warrior]] + [[Moment Of Triumph]], stir vigourously, and draw 2 extra destiny's. |combos=* [[Presence Of The Force]] + [[Endor Shield (V)]] + [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] Three Force icons for you, none for the Light Side. Opportunity to drain for three.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Presence%20Of%20The%20Force Scomp: Presence Of The Force]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Decipher (Reflections foil)''' — [[Presence Of The Force (Reflections Foil)|Presence Of The Force (foil)]] |sources=* Recreation of the Decipher.com Premiere Limited scan: white rounded border, transparent corners, same pixel size. * [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/index.html Premiere Dark Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Effect: Presence Of The Force, Premiere, R1 |strategy=By Justin Pakeshttps://web.archive.org/web/20001010191601/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/presenceoftheforce.html Imagine my dismay as I browsed the voluminous libraries of Deciphers card lists to discover that one of my favourite (proper English spelling there... :) cards was sans card extra. The often acronymed, PotF. So lets see if I can add anything to even that score. Being a Premiere card, the old hands amongst you may not find anything new here, but then again, maybe a refresher is in order. The card adds one red and one blue Force icon to whatever location you deploy it. A sabre for me, and a sabre for you. The deploy is zero as are the deployment restrictions. It's a two dot card, but remember that "cumulativity" stops you gaining any benefits from two copies at the same location. The wonderous thing about this card is it's elegant simplicity but amazing versatility. One use of the card is a boon to the early game. It is an extra Force activated. And in that frustrating game where the only time you see your locations is as destiny draws, that extra one can be vital. The most obvious offensive use of this card is immediately apparent, a bigger drain at a location, preferably one you already securely control! Lovely for you, added headache for your opponent! And never forget that it is *any* location. Handy if your opponent forgot to stock Cloud Cars and your trying to boost the benefit of your cloud superiority! "Just another drain bonus" some of you are saying, I can get that with a sabre! But with the advent of [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], the true value of a PotF used in this way was realised. Being an extra icon, and NOT a drain bonus (such as +1 to Force Drains) it is immune to that 'Bane of the Drain', [[Great Warrior]] (Jedi Test #1). The alternate use is a little more subtle. At a location where you have no force icons, this card is better than a spy. Sure, it can't go undercover, but it won't get snipered by the first weapon that comes along either. That extra icon allows you normal deploy, and is like the front door key to many LS starting locations. E.g. Massasi [[Hoth: Echo Command Center (War Room){{!}}War Room]], Obi's Hut, [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] Echo Base Command Centre (before the shields go up), or even LS [[Dantooine (Dark){{!}}Dantooine]]. If you can get the power down you need to hold them, that makes for a big early drain. If you have it in hand really early, it can be your only hope against those irritating LS decks that revolve your starting location early depriving you of force. Even better, allow yourself to get to that LS Big One and cancel that darned Asteroid Sanctuary. There are also a few more esoteric uses. A couple of cards are concerned with the number of icons at a location. [[Djas Puhr]], [[Feltipern Trevagg]], or even [[Commence Primary Ignition]] for a little added destruction. I would also say Braniac, but when it comes to that sort of mathematical proficiency, I'm a weak-minded fool. ;) "The perfect all round card!" I hear you now exclaim. Surely there's a catch! And indeed there is. But to me, the quality that makes this a *great* card is how it is a double-edged sabre if you use it without thinking. Very appopriate when you consider the picture on the card. Play it early, and you could be giving your opponent much needed Force activation. Put it on a location you cannot hold, and you may well feel the sting of the extra drain. Without proper planninng and situational analysis, many of the benefits could end up benefitting the Light Side. This tool belongs to the thinking player. And beware the counters too. Cloud City's Clash Of Sabres will cancel it outright. [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] has the same effect, but there's plenty of counter-counter's to that. And most irritating of all is [[I Have A Bad Feeling About This]] which LS can use to retarget it to a location they control (e.g. [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]!). I always recommend the multi-function [[Bad Feeling Have I]] to take care of that problem. Combos: How can you list combos for something that can be used almost anywhere, anytime? Obvious => PotF + LS Obi's Hut + your characters controlling it with a Vaders sabre and a Dark Jedi Sabre = drain of 6. Favourite => PotF + DS Mos Eisley + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Djas Puhr]] = An alien who even alone is Power 8, Ability 4, Forfeit 5, Immune To Attrition < 3, draws destiny, and gets an extra destiny worth of power! Even [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] would quietly thank the Emperor that he's on the right side of that behemoth! For icing on the attrition cake, add [[Lone Warrior]] + [[Moment Of Triumph]], stir vigourously, and draw 2 extra destiny's. |combos=* [[Presence Of The Force]] + [[Endor Shield (V)]] + [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] Three Force icons for you, none for the Light Side. Opportunity to drain for three.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Presence%20Of%20The%20Force Scomp: Presence Of The Force]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020174249/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json Internet Archive] Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009103048/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json Internet Archive primary-source copy]. |pulled_by=* [[Twi'lek Advisor]] * [[We Must Accelerate Our Plans]] |canceled_by=* [[Clash Of Sabers]] |also_known_as=* POTF |has_refs=1 }}

The often acronymed, PotF. So lets see if I can add anything to even that score. Being a Premiere card, the old hands amongst you may not find anything new here, but then again, maybe a refresher is in order. The card adds one red and one blue Force icon to whatever location you deploy it. A sabre for me, and a sabre for you. The deploy is zero as are the deployment restrictions. It's a two dot card, but remember that "cumulativity" stops you gaining any benefits from two copies at the same location. The wonderous thing about this card is it's elegant simplicity but amazing versatility. One use of the card is a boon to the early game. It is an extra Force activated. And in that frustrating game where the only time you see your locations is as destiny draws, that extra one can be vital. The most obvious offensive use of this card is immediately apparent, a bigger drain at a location, preferably one you already securely control! Lovely for you, added headache for your opponent! And never forget that it is *any* location. Handy if your opponent forgot to stock Cloud Cars and your trying to boost the benefit of your cloud superiority! "Just another drain bonus" some of you are saying, I can get that with a sabre! But with the advent of [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], the true value of a PotF used in this way was realised. Being an extra icon, and NOT a drain bonus (such as +1 to Force Drains) it is immune to that 'Bane of the Drain', [[Great Warrior]] (Jedi Test #1). The alternate use is a little more subtle. At a location where you have no force icons, this card is better than a spy. Sure, it can't go undercover, but it won't get snipered by the first weapon that comes along either. That extra icon allows you normal deploy, and is like the front door key to many LS starting locations. E.g. Massasi [[Hoth: Echo Command Center (War Room){{!}}War Room]], Obi's Hut, [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] Echo Base Command Centre (before the shields go up), or even LS [[Dantooine (Dark){{!}}Dantooine]]. If you can get the power down you need to hold them, that makes for a big early drain. If you have it in hand really early, it can be your only hope against those irritating LS decks that revolve your starting location early depriving you of force. Even better, allow yourself to get to that LS Big One and cancel that darned Asteroid Sanctuary. There are also a few more esoteric uses. A couple of cards are concerned with the number of icons at a location. [[Djas Puhr]], [[Feltipern Trevagg]], or even [[Commence Primary Ignition]] for a little added destruction. I would also say Braniac, but when it comes to that sort of mathematical proficiency, I'm a weak-minded fool. ;) "The perfect all round card!" I hear you now exclaim. Surely there's a catch! And indeed there is. But to me, the quality that makes this a *great* card is how it is a double-edged sabre if you use it without thinking. Very appopriate when you consider the picture on the card. Play it early, and you could be giving your opponent much needed Force activation. Put it on a location you cannot hold, and you may well feel the sting of the extra drain. Without proper planninng and situational analysis, many of the benefits could end up benefitting the Light Side. This tool belongs to the thinking player. And beware the counters too. Cloud City's Clash Of Sabres will cancel it outright. [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] has the same effect, but there's plenty of counter-counter's to that. And most irritating of all is [[I Have A Bad Feeling About This]] which LS can use to retarget it to a location they control (e.g. [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]!). I always recommend the multi-function [[Bad Feeling Have I]] to take care of that problem. Combos: How can you list combos for something that can be used almost anywhere, anytime? Obvious => PotF + LS Obi's Hut + your characters controlling it with a Vaders sabre and a Dark Jedi Sabre = drain of 6. Favourite => PotF + DS Mos Eisley + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Djas Puhr]] = An alien who even alone is Power 8, Ability 4, Forfeit 5, Immune To Attrition < 3, draws destiny, and gets an extra destiny worth of power! Even [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] would quietly thank the Emperor that he's on the right side of that behemoth! For icing on the attrition cake, add [[Lone Warrior]] + [[Moment Of Triumph]], stir vigourously, and draw 2 extra destiny's. |combos=* [[Presence Of The Force]] + [[Endor Shield (V)]] + [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] Three Force icons for you, none for the Light Side. Opportunity to drain for three.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Presence%20Of%20The%20Force Scomp: Presence Of The Force]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020174249/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json Internet Archive] Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009103048/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json Internet Archive primary-source copy]. |pulled_by=* [[Twi'lek Advisor]] * [[We Must Accelerate Our Plans]] |canceled_by=* [[Clash Of Sabers]] |also_known_as=* POTF |has_refs=1 }}

Title: R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo) Lore:
A small-bodied droid brimming with energy, loyal to his master and brave. A Rebel spy who is strong in adversity. Though 3PO derided him as a “cold-hearted philosopher,” his personality is rather the opposite. He is somewhat restless and sometimes acts unexpectedly.
Card text:
Adds +2 to the power, maneuver and hyperspeed of the starfighter he is aboard (+3 if Red 5). When he is at a place with an access link and the opponent draws destiny, activate 1 Force if it is 1–3. If it is 4–6, draw the top card of the Reserve Deck and add it to your hand.
=== Comparison with the English printing === The Japanese lore says that 3PO derided R2-D2 as a “cold-hearted philosopher”; the English face instead calls R2-D2 the “Incorrigible counterpart of a mindless philosopher.” The Japanese game text uses アクセス・リンク (access link) for the English Scomp link and states the two results directly, without words corresponding to the English “you may.” It expressly adds the drawn Reserve Deck card to the hand. The printed numerical statistics match the inspected English face. Neither inspected face prints a Nav Computer symbol; a later rule-derived capability must not be presented as a printed icon.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 42 (Japanese card face), pp. 101–102 (checklist). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]. The comparison uses the [[:File:ANH-L-r2d2.gif|original English card face]]. |see_also=* [[R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)|English counterpart]] * [[A New Hope (Japanese)#Card list|Japanese A New Hope card list]] * [[Translations of SWCCG#Japanese|Japanese printings]] |see_also_heading=See also |has_refs=1 |extra_sections=

Statistics

The printed values and symbols are shown above. The face prints one Droid symbol and the subtype 操縦ドロイド (astromech droid). It has no printed ability number and no printed Nav Computer, Pilot or Warrior symbol. Its lore identifies a Rebel spy.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 42 (Japanese card face), pp. 101–102 (checklist). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]. Base landspeed is 1 under the character movement rule; this is a rule-derived value, not a printed statistic.[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game RULEBOOK 2.0#Landspeed|Rulebook 2.0, Landspeed]]: “Characters have landspeed of 1.” The 1998 Glossary states that astromech droids provide nav computers. This is a rule-derived capability, separate from the absence of a printed Nav Computer symbol on this face.[[:File:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary (1998)]], pp. 15 and 94, “astromech” and “nav computer icon”. The same Glossary gives droids no ability and gives droids without armor a defense value of zero.[[:File:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary (1998)]], p. 52, “droid”. |set_icon=[[File:Icon-set-A-New-Hope.png|20px|link=A New Hope Limited]] [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] }}

Its what the Rebel Alliance is all about! This Effect from the Premiere Edition has endured, and even grown in popularity through all the game expansions. Many players find it an indispensable tool in the battle to overthrow the Empire. A list of the benefits of [[Revolution]]: 1) it can be deployed on any location (except the [[Death Star]]) 2) it Revolves (switches) not only the game text, but also the Force icons at that location, 3) although it is not cumulative, there is no limit to how many [[Revolution]] cards can be in play. When the Premiere Edition stood alone, [[Revolution]] was used most often as a way to increase Light Side Force drains. Played on [[Tatooine: Obi-Wan's Hut]], it created an easy Force drain of 3. This strategy is still prevalent, but now many players rely on [[Revolution]] at [[Dagobah: Yoda's Hut]] to create a Force drain that is difficult to counter. Equally important is the strategy of using [[Revolution]] to take away game text and Force icons from the Dark Side. Deploying a couple of Revolutions early in the game can cripple Dark Side ground-based decks such as [[Walker Garrison]] or [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] drain, by denying them both Force generation and Force drain bonuses. [[Revolution]] has a destiny of 3, pretty average, and a fairly high deploy cost of 3. The main drawbacks of this card are the new cards that Decipher has created, which specifically counteract the powerful effects of [[Revolution]]. The Light Side player must be prepared with multiple [[Sense]] and [[Control]] cards to defend [[Revolution]] against [[Evader]] or [[Surprise]] , and may find it impossible to counter the very popular [[Imperial Decree]]. On a positive note, [[Revolution]] is not cancelled by [[Imperial Decree]], just "ignored." Late in a game, if the Light Side prevails and the conditions for [[Imperial Decree]] cannot be met, the Dark Side will suffer the effects of [[Revolution]] again! Card Combos: [[Revolution]] + any Hut for a significant Force drain bonus. [[Revolution]] versus the [[Tatooine: Jundland Wastes]] + Expand the Empire card combo: Make the Dark Side regret using this popular Force drain strategy. [[Revolution]] is one of the few cards that can make a Dark Side Effect work for the Light Side. |combos=* [[Revolution]] + any Hut Significant Force drain bonus.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Revolution Scomp: Revolution]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Its what the Rebel Alliance is all about! This Effect from the Premiere Edition has endured, and even grown in popularity through all the game expansions. Many players find it an indispensable tool in the battle to overthrow the Empire. A list of the benefits of [[Revolution]]: 1) it can be deployed on any location (except the [[Death Star]]) 2) it Revolves (switches) not only the game text, but also the Force icons at that location, 3) although it is not cumulative, there is no limit to how many [[Revolution]] cards can be in play. When the Premiere Edition stood alone, [[Revolution]] was used most often as a way to increase Light Side Force drains. Played on [[Tatooine: Obi-Wan's Hut]], it created an easy Force drain of 3. This strategy is still prevalent, but now many players rely on [[Revolution]] at [[Dagobah: Yoda's Hut]] to create a Force drain that is difficult to counter. Equally important is the strategy of using [[Revolution]] to take away game text and Force icons from the Dark Side. Deploying a couple of Revolutions early in the game can cripple Dark Side ground-based decks such as [[Walker Garrison]] or [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] drain, by denying them both Force generation and Force drain bonuses. [[Revolution]] has a destiny of 3, pretty average, and a fairly high deploy cost of 3. The main drawbacks of this card are the new cards that Decipher has created, which specifically counteract the powerful effects of [[Revolution]]. The Light Side player must be prepared with multiple [[Sense]] and [[Control]] cards to defend [[Revolution]] against [[Evader]] or [[Surprise]] , and may find it impossible to counter the very popular [[Imperial Decree]]. On a positive note, [[Revolution]] is not cancelled by [[Imperial Decree]], just "ignored." Late in a game, if the Light Side prevails and the conditions for [[Imperial Decree]] cannot be met, the Dark Side will suffer the effects of [[Revolution]] again! Card Combos: [[Revolution]] + any Hut for a significant Force drain bonus. [[Revolution]] versus the [[Tatooine: Jundland Wastes]] + Expand the Empire card combo: Make the Dark Side regret using this popular Force drain strategy. [[Revolution]] is one of the few cards that can make a Dark Side Effect work for the Light Side. |combos=* [[Revolution]] + any Hut Significant Force drain bonus.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Revolution Scomp: Revolution]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec).
