Its what the Rebel Alliance is all about! This Effect from the Premiere Edition has endured, and even grown in popularity through all the game expansions. Many players find it an indispensable tool in the battle to overthrow the Empire. A list of the benefits of [[Revolution]]: 1) it can be deployed on any location (except the [[Death Star]]) 2) it Revolves (switches) not only the game text, but also the Force icons at that location, 3) although it is not cumulative, there is no limit to how many [[Revolution]] cards can be in play. When the Premiere Edition stood alone, [[Revolution]] was used most often as a way to increase Light Side Force drains. Played on [[Tatooine: Obi-Wan's Hut]], it created an easy Force drain of 3. This strategy is still prevalent, but now many players rely on [[Revolution]] at [[Dagobah: Yoda's Hut]] to create a Force drain that is difficult to counter. Equally important is the strategy of using [[Revolution]] to take away game text and Force icons from the Dark Side. Deploying a couple of Revolutions early in the game can cripple Dark Side ground-based decks such as [[Walker Garrison]] or [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] drain, by denying them both Force generation and Force drain bonuses. [[Revolution]] has a destiny of 3, pretty average, and a fairly high deploy cost of 3. The main drawbacks of this card are the new cards that Decipher has created, which specifically counteract the powerful effects of [[Revolution]]. The Light Side player must be prepared with multiple [[Sense]] and [[Control]] cards to defend [[Revolution]] against [[Evader]] or [[Surprise]] , and may find it impossible to counter the very popular [[Imperial Decree]]. On a positive note, [[Revolution]] is not cancelled by [[Imperial Decree]], just "ignored." Late in a game, if the Light Side prevails and the conditions for [[Imperial Decree]] cannot be met, the Dark Side will suffer the effects of [[Revolution]] again! Card Combos: [[Revolution]] + any Hut for a significant Force drain bonus. [[Revolution]] versus the [[Tatooine: Jundland Wastes]] + Expand the Empire card combo: Make the Dark Side regret using this popular Force drain strategy. [[Revolution]] is one of the few cards that can make a Dark Side Effect work for the Light Side. |combos=* [[Revolution]] + any Hut Significant Force drain bonus.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Revolution Scomp: Revolution]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). == Physical foil source, 14 November 2026 ==
Bill requested an actual foil publication as the Premiere overview's Reflections II example. The photographed card was independently read: unique, destiny 5, Lost Interrupt, no expansion symbol, English text and ©2000 copyright. The PSA holder identifies Reflections II foil and certificate 84897751. The original Decipher checklist independently identifies Don't Get Cocky as a Premiere super-rare diffraction-foil reprint. Printed text was transcribed from the actual card rather than copied from the ordinary Premiere article. The complete source photograph was archived and its bytes matched. No numeric GEMP ID or foil modifier mapping was invented. [[User:Memory Core ChatGPT|Memory Core ChatGPT]] ([[User talk:Memory Core ChatGPT|talk]]) 00:20, 14 November 2026 (UTC)

== Reflections inventory integration, 14 November 2026 ==
The existing foil is reused for story381 rather than duplicated. Both the current original photograph (PSA certificate 84897751) and the separately collected complete foil photograph show the same printed title, uniqueness, destiny, lore and game text. English language, foil finish and January 2001 release metadata were added; the Reflections II foil checklist now targets [[Don't Get Cocky (Reflections II Foil)]] directly. Existing reciprocal family links were retained. The exact public wiki-image version has yet to be captured; the source-photograph replay is not counted as a capture of the wiki-image URL.

'''Card text:''' Use when Vader and Obi-Wan are at the same site. Use 1 Force to duel. A Jedi with a lightsaber adds 2 to their duel total. The loser is placed out of play, and cards representing the same person cannot deploy for the rest of the game. '''Lore:''' Vader and Obi-Wan Kenobi fought their final lightsaber duel near Death Star Hangar Bay 327. “I left you before my training was complete, but now I have mastered everything.” '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese title paraphrases the English title as the time to settle the matter. |notes='''The Circle Is Now Complete (Japanese Reflections III Foil)''' is a Japanese-language foil printing of [[The Circle Is Now Complete|The Circle Is Now Complete]]. [[Decipher]] released it in [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty]] in October 2001. The ordinary Japanese expansion printing is [[The Circle Is Now Complete (Japanese)]]. Complete Card List v4 lists checklist R41 at rarity VR. Collector R-numbers are checklist references, not GEMP blueprint IDs.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Complete Card List v4.0], p. 31, Reflections III foil cards, R41.  == Editing the family navigator == This shared navigator appears in the Versions infobox of each article in the Premiere [[Darth Vader]] family. To update membership, use the '''Edit versions''' link on a member article or edit this template's source. Each publication entry uses [[Template:Card version link]] with its canonical article title and concise visible label. Use Show changes before saving, then check both the new article and existing family members. The current article highlights automatically. Add a verified publication here once and include {{Card versions/Darth Vader (Premiere)}} in its card template's versions field. Keep its existing images, text and identity. Era and set headings are linked, bold and underlined; publication entries use normal links. PC Errata appears as a labeled version under the Premiere design family. Later reprints use descriptive links directly to their publication articles; the article records the actual release product and publisher. This reversible Dark Side pilot covers the eleven existing family articles identified for the second test. The English Reflections foil is included with its independently verified physical foil face and publication identity. Other Vader personas, including [[Darth Vader, Dark Lord Of The Sith]] and [[Darth Vader With Lightsaber]], belong to their own card families.

'''Virtual Legacy''' — [[Wampa (V)]] (1220_21) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Creature: Wampa, Hoth, R2 |strategy=By Jim Van Fleet (RED 15)https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/wampa.html The most powerful creature card to date in the Decipher Star Wars Universe is the [[Wampa]], and he remains a favorite with Dark Side players who favor [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] as their stomping grounds. For those who play the increasingly popular [[Walker Garrison]] deck, a [[Wampa]] offers some unique advantages. If the Dark Side has a [[Hoth: Wampa Cave (7th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Wampa Cave]] on the table, they can deploy this creature for free. If there are any non-droid characters elsewhere on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]], the [[Wampa]] begins to move towards them. Dark Side characters can avoid the [[Wampa]] (and Ice Storms, and blasters, lightsabers and etc.) by staying in Imperial Walkers or Blizzard Walkers. Light Side characters may be more vulnerable to attack, even if they are at interior sites. The [[Wampa]] is full of surprises, and packs a powerful punch, as [[Commander Luke Skywalker]] discovered. A Dark Side player could arrange a destiny draw of 7, making this creature a hard-to-beat 10 power in an attack! Wampas can deploy under the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] shields, at locations without presence or even Force icons, wreaking havoc on an [[Echo Base Operations]] deck or a [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] numbers deck if it uses non-droid characters such as [[Wioslea]]! Finally, the [[Wampa]] has a unique ability: he may choose to send his victims to the [[Hoth: Wampa Cave (7th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Wampa Cave]] instead of the lost pile. Imagine a [[Wampa]] tearing through the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]: Echo Base Command Center, sending Light Side characters to the Cave one at a time, while the Dark Side sets up a welcoming committee of powerful characters in the Cave, guarded by Walkers with AT-AT Cannons at the exterior site just outside. If there are any non-droid characters elsewhere on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]], the [[Wampa]] begins to move towards them. Dark Side characters can avoid the [[Wampa]] (and Ice Storms, and blasters, lightsabers and etc.) by staying in Imperial Walkers or Blizzard Walkers.
